messages.author: d25ec8b43762536f
messages.subject: Tide parameters in microclimate
parts:
Hi everyone,
Now I want to use NichemapR-microclimate to predict intertidal microenvironmental data. This requires the input parameter Tides. But the Tides given in the document seems to have no practical significance.

# intertidal simulation input vector (col 1 = tide in(1)/out(0), col 2 = sea water temperature in °C, col 3 = % wet from wave splash)
tides <- matrix(data = 0, nrow = 24 * doynum, ncol = 3) # matrix for tides

And I'm not sure about the format of col1 and col3 and how they will be entered.

Thank You.

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Tide parameters in microclimate
parts:
Hi - the tides simulation is not well tested so it will be worth having some real data to assess how well it works. It tries to capture the effect of water coming in over the substrate by simulating a very strong convective connection to the water temperature by making the wind speed arbitrarily high (50000 m/s!) and having only convection and conduction involved in the heat budget when the tide is in.

When you say the tides given in the document have no practical significance, I presume you're referring to the fact that by default an empty matrix is passed. That is to prevent a tidal simulation from occurring by default. As the instructions say though, you just make a matrix where the first column consists of 1 or 0 indicating whether the tide is in or out that hour, column 2 is the sea water temperature in deg C, and column 3 is a number that indicates the percentage wetness of the surface if you want to simulate a situation where waves are splashing the site of interest.

Does that help?

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 75ea8422851125e3
messages.subject: Re: Tide parameters in microclimate
parts:
If you want a true tide model, you could consider xtide (https://flaterco.com/).  This program comes with tidal constituents for a reasonably large number of sites around the world.  The command-line tool  xtide in the package can be run with a system() call in R.  If you are working in the USA, the rtide package can be useful - it has constituents from NOAA.  

You can get seawater temperature from one of the L4 (cloud-free) datasets like the UK MetOffice global daily 5km scale SST, available from marine.copernicus.eu (product  SST_GLO_SST_L4_NRT_OBSERVATIONS_010_001 ) or from  podaac.jpl.nasa.gov
(product  OSTIA-UKMO-L4-GLOB-v2.0).  The near real-time product covers the period 2007-present, and the reanalysis product (available only from marine.copernicus.eu) covers the period back to 1982.  An alternative is the CCI-SST which is a carefully curated, de-biased, and homogenized L4 5km global daily cloud free SST climate data record from the European Space Agency: https://climate.esa.int/en/projects/sea-surface-temperature/ 1982-present. Higher spatial resolution products exist for shorter time periods and smaller geographic regions.  See the GHRSST product collection at PODAAC.

David Wethey
